claims.text: Premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding is caused by elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
A roughly 50–100 nm CrN interlayer will act as an effective barrier to Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
CrN and Cr/CrN are candidate protective-coating materials for zirconium-alloy accident-tolerant cladding.
The CrN interlayer will prevent premature coating failure.
The CrN interlayer will preserve protection during normal subcritical-water reactor operation.
The CrN interlayer will preserve oxidation protection during accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
High-temperature steam oxidation resistance is a critical requirement for zirconium-alloy accident-tolerant cladding.
Approximately 700–800 °C is the relevant target range for the proposed accident-transient protection.
The CrN interlayer will remain continuous, dense, and chemically stable during the specified exposures.
CrN presents a high-activation-energy barrier to the diffusion of Cr and Zr atoms.
Suppressing Cr and Zr diffusion will limit the formation of deleterious intermetallic phases at the interface.
Limiting interdiffusion and intermetallic formation will preserve coating mechanical integrity and oxidation resistance.
Relative to directly applied Cr, the CrN-interlayer system will have a significantly thinner Cr–Zr interdiffusion zone.
Relative to directly applied Cr, the CrN-interlayer system will exhibit enhanced coating adhesion and less cracking.
Relative to directly applied Cr, the CrN-interlayer system will exhibit improved high-temperature oxidation performance.
The proposed effectiveness is bounded to approximately 700–800 °C and loss-of-coolant-accident transient durations.
A controlled comparison at 750 °C for 2 hours, supplemented by simulated subcritical-water exposure, can discriminate the modified coating from the directly applied Cr baseline.
